episodes.181524: Abundant monsoon moisture remained across Western Colorado. This led to another round of showers and thunderstorms across much of the region. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. As a result of the heavy rain, some flash flooding and debris flows occurred in Mesa and Eagle counties. Additionally, gusty outflow winds in excess of 58 mph occurred across portions of the Western Slope. The passage of a weak trough across northwest Colorado resulted in some stronger storms. One storm in Routt County produced a funnel cloud.
episodes.181546: A line of storms moving across the Four Corners area produced dry microbursts and significant damage at several locations across the Northwest Plateau in northwest NM. The Farmington observing station reported a wind gust of 50 knots or 58 miles per hour on the leading edge of the storms.
episodes.181569: A low pressure system moved up from the south, tapped into monsoonal moisture, and produced strong thunderstorms with heavy rainfall.
episodes.181572: Drier air began to work into eastern Utah in the wake of a recent monsoon surge. Even so, enough residual moisture was present to fuel isolated thunderstorms. Some storms produced wind gusts in excess of 58 mph in Grand County.
episodes.181574: Heavy rain from slow-moving thunderstorms produced localized flooding as well as gusty winds.
episodes.181576: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms erupted during the midday into mid afternoon hours along and south of the Tennessee River. These thunderstorms pushed south-southeast, producing wind damage in Morgan, Cullman and Marshall Counties. Numerous trees were knocked down, and some structural damage was reported.
episodes.181653: A weak cold front dropped south across central Wisconsin on the evening of August 3rd, producing a broken line of stronger storms which impacted portions of the Lake Michigan shoreline near Sheboygan.
episodes.181687: Severe thunderstorms produced strong winds and flash flooding across parts of southeast Wyoming on 3 August 2023.
episodes.181764: Thunderstorms repeatedly developed along an instability gradient across northeast Wisconsin along the Michigan border from the late afternoon through the evening hours and produced strong winds as they traveled over the bay of Green Bay and Lake Michigan waters on Wednesday (8/2).
episodes.181765: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the late afternoon and evening hours across east-central Wisconsin.  The strongest storms produced damaging winds and quarter size hail. The storms heavily damaged a golf clubhouse in Wrightstown.
episodes.181766: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the afternoon and evening hours.  These storms produced strong winds and large hail as they tracked over the bay of Green Bay and Lake Michigan waters.
episodes.182081: Severe thunderstorms impacted portions of northeastern Mississippi in early August. Scattered wind damage occurred with storms on several afternoons between August 3rd and 5th.
episodes.182286: A complex of thunderstorms moved southeast across eastern Missouri during the early nighttime hours. A portion of this complex evolved into a bowing line, producing damaging winds in parts of southeast Missouri to the north and northwest of Cape Girardeau. The storms occurred in the vicinity of a warm front that extended east-northeast from a low pressure center over the Oklahoma panhandle. The activity was aided by a very unstable feed of air from the southwest, with mixed-layer cape of 3000-3500 J/kg. Northwest flow of 30 to 40 knots in the middle levels of the atmosphere supported the bowing line of storms.
episodes.182331: A line of rain showers was moving eastward along a frontal boundary during the afternoon. A brief spin up tornado occurred with one of these stronger rain showers within an area of weak rotation across eastern Roane County near the Oral community. Severe downdraft winds occurred sporadically in association with this briefly tornadic thunderstorm.
episodes.183046: Two separate clusters of thunderstorms developed during the early morning hours of August 3rd, one over central Nebraska and another in the area of the Colorado, Nebraska, and Kansas border. The two thunderstorm clusters conjoined into one as they moved towards Highway 283 between 5-6AM CDT. This activity was largely elevated in nature to the north of a surface warm front that was draped west to east just south of the Nebraska-Kansas state line. However, a small portion of the cluster became surface based, at least briefly, over portions of Phelps County where severe wind gusts and damage were reported between 6-7 AM CDT. It appears a microburst occurred just south and southwest of Holdrege given a narrow corridor of damage that included overturned pivots and tree and grain bin damage. A mesonet also measured a wind gust of 78 MPH in the vicinity of the damage. Thunderstorms weakened substantially between 7-8 AM CDT as they moved east across south central Nebraska.
episodes.183548: Northwest to southeast oriented bands of thunderstorms moved southeast, training over the same areas for several hours. A strong and very moist low-level wind flow fed the storms, with 850 mb winds generally from 35 to 40 knots. Tropical precipitable water values were estimated to be between 2 and 2.4 inches. Instability was sufficient for strong updrafts, with 1000 to 2000 J/kg of elevated cape near the confluence of the Ohio and Mississippi Rivers. The focus for the heaviest rain was from southeastern Missouri into far western Kentucky, northeast of a surface warm front draped across the central Missouri/Arkansas border.
episodes.183549: A large complex of thunderstorms stagnated over parts of southern Illinois, along and north of Interstate 64. Thunderstorms trained across those areas within an environment highly capable of producing high rainfall rates. Precipitable water values ranged between 2 and 2.5 inches, along with modest instability (500 to 1500 J/kg of elevated cape). The axis of thunderstorms occurred northeast of a surface boundary over southwestern Missouri, along an elevated convergence axis. The steering flow was nearly parallel to the convergence axis, supporting training and repeating of storm cells. A remnant mesoscale convective vorticity center over western Illinois advanced southeast in the northwest mid-level flow. This feature helped initiate thunderstorms through the night.
episodes.183550: Northwest to southeast oriented bands of thunderstorms moved southeast, training over the same areas for several hours. A strong and very moist low-level wind flow fed the storms, with 850 mb winds generally from 35 to 40 knots. Tropical precipitable water values were estimated to be between 2 and 2.4 inches. Instability was sufficient for strong updrafts, with 1000 to 2000 J/kg of elevated cape near the confluence of the Ohio and Mississippi Rivers. The focus for the heaviest rain was from southeastern Missouri into far western Kentucky, northeast of a surface warm front draped across the central Missouri/Arkansas border.
episodes.183553: Thunderstorms repeatedly generated over parts of southwest Indiana along a convergence axis in the mid levels of the atmosphere. A remnant upper-level disturbance over western Illinois moved southeast, providing support for the storms. The atmosphere was very moist, with precipitable water values over 2 inches.
episodes.183589: A stationary front draped across southern Missouri and far southern Illinois aided thunderstorm development, including a narrow band of training thunderstorms across southeast Illinois during the early morning hours of August 3. These thunderstorms resulted in heavy rainfall, with reports ranging from 2 to 7 inches across Clay County, which led to flash flooding.
episodes.183940: Thunderstorms along a slow moving cold front produced damaging winds to portions of Fond du Lac and Sheboygan Counties.
episodes.184036: Remnants of thunderstorms in Tennessee moved into North Georgia in the early afternoon hours of the 3rd. Meanwhile, daytime heating across Central Georgia helped to destabilize the moist airmass in place. Thunderstorms began to redevelop into a Mesoscale Convective Complex (MCS) developing severe winds across a broad area.
episodes.184523: Several severe thunderstorms developed over the Thumb region, producing strong winds which brought down trees.
episodes.184527: Thunderstorms moving through Saginaw Bay produced wind gusts around 40 knots.
episodes.184641: A strong thunderstorm produced hail up to nickel size near Erie.
episodes.184642: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail, ranging from quarter to golfball size, across portions of Adams, Denver, Elbert, Larimer, Logan and Weld counties.  In addition, a few of the storms produced peak wind gusts from 64 to 68 mph.
episodes.184697: A cluster of training showers and thunderstorms affected portions of Addison and northwestern Windsor Counties on the evening of August 3, 2023 leading to areas of flash flooding, some severe. Three to as much as six inches of rain were recorded in these areas with the Town of Middlebury, VT being the hardest hit. A wet microburst in the Middlebury area also produced localized wind damage.
episodes.184790: A stationary front was located from Kansas into the Mid-South during the morning hours of August 3, 2023. A nocturnal low-level jet transported moist and unstable air into this stalled boundary. As a result, a mesoscale convective system developed over Missouri and moved east-southeast into northwest Tennessee along the frontal boundary. Heavy rainfall across parts of northwest Tennessee resulted in flash flooding.
episodes.184843: A slow moving low pressure system brought multiple rounds of scattered showers and thunderstorms across eastern New York from August 3 to August 4, 2023. Isolated thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours on August 3 in the system's warm sector producing locally damaging wind gusts, small hail and also a funnel cloud. Additional thunderstorm activity developed ahead of a cold front during the morning hours on August 4, especially across Herkimer County, with activity shifting eastward into the Hudson Valley during the afternoon and evening. Additional wind damage and large hail was observed with these storms as well as localized areas of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.184926: An active northwest upper flow pattern produced several waves of convective storms during the first week of August.
episodes.184949: A deep monsoonal event impacted Utah at the beginning of August. Each of these days across northern Utah, widespread thunderstorms and flooding impacted the region. Very heavy rainfall impacted West Valley City, Honeyville, and Draper in particular.
episodes.184960: A complex of non-severe thunderstorms rolled through Central Kansas during the night of 3 August and the morning of 4 August.  Very heavy rain occurred during this event producing rainfall amounts ranging from 1 to nearly 3 inches.
episodes.184964: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed in the late afternoon into the evening along a slow moving to nearly stationary frontal boundary. As storms moved across central Missouri Additional rainfall fell over areas that received rain the previous day and earlier in the morning of the 3rd. Hail up to golf balls in size were reported with the strongest updrafts in central Missouri.
episodes.185129: Monsoon like conditions existed over the western half of the US with some of the thunderstorms that developed over Pueblo's mountains developing into a better environment for severe weather.
episodes.185146: An upper level disturbance moved into a moderately unstable airmass across northern NY during the afternoon of August 3rd. Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed in the Adirondacks and moved into the Champlain Valley.  A few storms produced locally large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.185316: A shortwave trough punched over the northern Great Lakes on 8/3, providing favorable forcing aloft to support scattered thunderstorm development amidst ample instability in place during the afternoon. These storms produced severe hail over northern Lake Huron and portions of northwest lower Michigan, as well as measured severe wind gusts near the Traverse City area.
episodes.185317: A shortwave trough punched over the northern Great Lakes on 8/3, providing favorable forcing aloft to support scattered thunderstorm development amidst ample instability in place during the afternoon. One of these storms produced golf ball sized hail over far northern Lake Huron that was reported aboard the Joseph L. Block freighter.
episodes.185318: A shortwave trough punched over the northern Great Lakes on 8/3, providing favorable forcing aloft to support scattered thunderstorm development amidst ample instability in place during the afternoon. A cluster of these storm produced wind gusts in excess of 60 mph over Grand Traverse Bay.
episodes.185362: A line of thunderstorms moved into northeast Georgia during the late afternoon. An embedded cell within this line produced a weak tornado that tracked across parts of three counties. Some isolated gusty winds were also reported.
episodes.185363: An area of rain showers with scattered embedded thunderstorm moved across the South Carolina foothills during the late afternoon. The storms produced a couple of short tack, weak tornadoes in Pickens County.
episodes.185417: Increasing moisture and instability from the southwest led to scattered thunderstorms across the mountainous terrain of eastern Oregon. One of these storms was strong enough to produce large hail across southeastern Grant County.
episodes.185496: On the evening of August 2nd, a discrete storm brought quarter sized hail to the small town of Windsor in Pettis County.
episodes.185557: Waterspout observed over eastern Tampa Bay northwest of Apollo Beach with evening convection.
episodes.185636: A couple thunderstorms developed during the evening of August 03 across east central Minnesota. One thunderstorm produced a microburst that caused damage to a pontoon  boat and dock. There were no other reports of damage.
episodes.186343: Thunderstorms developed over central Missouri during the early evening hours. They moved east/southeast through the overnight hours. Numerous large hail and damaging wind reports were received. During the late evening through overnight hours, widespread heavy rain fell causing flash flooding. There was fairly widespread 1-3 rainfall totals, with isolated 6-8+ in central Missouri and south-central Illinois.
episodes.186344: Thunderstorms developed over central Missouri during the early evening hours. They moved east/southeast through the overnight hours. Numerous large hail and damaging wind reports were received. During the late evening through overnight hours, widespread heavy rain fell causing flash flooding. There was fairly widespread 1-3 rainfall totals, with isolated 6-8+ in central Missouri and south-central Illinois.

events.narrative: The Colorado Department of Transportation reported flash flooding on Colorado Highway 340 at the west entrance to the Colorado National Monument. Up to 6 inches of water ran across the road as a result of heavy from thunderstorms. Additionally, some large boulder collapsed on the road as well as some mud. The superintendent of the Colorado National Monument also reported several inches of water flooded the Visitor's Center. Luckily, there were no injuries or damage to cars reported during the event. The rain gauge, located across from the Visitor's Center, recorded 0.90 inches of rain in 20 minutes.

This caused Camp Creek to rise well above it's banks, flooding Camp Creek Court at the intersection with Colony Church Road. A motorist drove their vehicle into the flood waters and became stranded. They were rescued and did not sustain any injuries.

The tornado touched down in the community of Oral in eastern Roane County near the intersection of country lane and Highway 70. The tornado tracked eastward along Highway 70 for a half mile before dissipating near Oral Cemetery. The most significant damage occurred near the beginning of the track where a small detached garage was destroyed and debris strewn about 100 yards in different directions. A few trees were uprooted and homes and fences suffered minor damage. As the tornado continued east, damage was mainly limited to small branches broken from trees. Dissipation at Oral Cemetery was noted with a metal roof sheet laying in the cemetery and an end to minor vegetation damage.
